question:
Select the most appropriate homonym.

He was __charged __with theft.
solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 4** i.e. **Accused**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Charged"** has multiple meanings depending on the context. In this sentence, it refers to being formally accused of a crime. (आरोपित)

 
 
• **Example:** The man was charged with theft after being caught with stolen goods.
 
 
 
• **"Accused"** means someone who is blamed or formally charged with a wrongdoing or a crime. (आरोपी)
 
 
• **Example:** The accused was presented before the court for trial.
 
 
 
• In the given sentence, "charged" aligns with "accused" since it refers to a formal allegation of theft. Hence, "Accused" is the most appropriate homonym.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 4** i.e. **Accused**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Energized** (ऊर्जावान): To give energy or enthusiasm to something or someone.

 
 
• **Example:** The motivational speech energized the entire team before the match.
 
 
 
• **Filled** (भरा हुआ): To make or become full of something.
 
 
• **Example:** Her eyes were filled with tears of joy after hearing the good news.
 
 
 
• **Ordered** (आदेशित): To command or instruct someone to do something.
 
 
• **Example:** The manager ordered the team to complete the project by the end of the week.
 
 

**Note: **This is a PYP Question.
